To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
The meaning and purposes of accountability are the same at national and transnational scales, and accountability can serve as both a stabilizer of governance and a catalyst for change.
accountability in transnational governance is a means for legitimizing and stabilising public governance processes, for political contestation, and for institutional change.

In summary, our research is concerned with
the meaning, purposes, and practices of accountability in transnational governance.
how accountability operates as a mechanism of political and institutional contestation, and how it is used to promote institutional change.
how transnational accountability can help to shape the political and institutional landscape of transnational governance.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

accountability in the transnational context is a complex, contested and evolving concept, which is not only relevant to transnational governance, but can also provide a valuable lens to understand and analyse transnational governance.
the meaning of accountability is the same at national and transnational scale but the purposes of accountability may be different.
accountability is not a ‘one size fits all’ solution to problems of transnational governance; rather, the meaning and purposes of accountability must be understood and analysed in context.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
accountability is a process through which an actor (individual or institution) justifies or explains actions and holds others to an account for them.

the concept of transnational accountability is useful for understanding and analysing the ways in which transnational governance processes are legitimized and stabilized, but also for analysing the political contestation and change that may be triggered by transnational accountability processes.
accountability is a process of answering for conduct through which power is exercised.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the meaning and purposes of transnational accountability cannot be understood by simply applying the same concepts that have been used to analyse accountability at national scale.
transnational extension of accountability is not necessarily an ‘overstretch’, but rather an opportunity for a more nuanced and critical understanding of accountability’s purposes.
the meaning and purpose of accountability are not static. Rather, the meaning of accountability is contingent on the context of its use.
